## 1 · ⭐ The `#8344` `superRefine` clause is DEAD AT RUNTIME on the new head, not merely redundant

`defineNodeComponentUnion` (`packages/types/src/zod/base.zod.ts`) installs a `superRefine` clause that re-issues the node-slot's own issues under `body` for a `chatbot` node. Reviewer's reading at head `24b009d088`:

- the nested refusal's issue tree carries **the arm's tombstone and no clause-shaped issue** — zod skips the check once the arm has refused, and the clause returns early on `undefined`;
- at the merge base the clause's `body.0.body` issue **was** the refusal.

⇒ once `ChatbotSchema.body` is a tombstone, the clause can no longer fire for the only key it was written for. It is retained **only** because `node-recursion-point-8344.test.ts`'s `fill is LIVE` leg asserts the wrapper carries exactly one check.

⚠️ **This seat was wrong about this once already, and the correction matters for whoever takes the card.** Earlier this shift the seat told the #8572 dev it would file a card for this guard, then read the tree and found the dev's own ruling — "dead-code class, filing rules exclude it" — was right for the question as it stood then, and sent an explicit correction. The reviewer's claim is a **different** one: not "this code is unreachable so delete it" but "a PIN now asserts the shape of an inert clause". ⛔ Do not read the earlier correction as covering this.

Suggested disposition (⛔ not a ruling): retire the clause and re-point the `fill is LIVE` pin at the installation itself, so the pin keeps testing that slot 0 holds the WRAPPED union — which is what it is really for — without pinning a clause nobody can make fire.

## 2 · The `names body in the refusal` leg is VACUOUS for the chatbot key

Same file. That leg reads the nested document, whose **parent card slot already puts `"body"` in the issue path for any refused child** — so the assertion passes whether or not the chatbot arm names anything. Pre-existing from objectui#8344, unchanged by #9639, and now covered anyway by the inverted root pin's `path === 'body'` assertion.

⇒ re-point it at something that can fail, or drop it. ⛔ A leg that cannot fail is not coverage; it is a green light wired to nothing.

## 3 · The plain `chatbot` row in the 9256 narrowing table lost its same-face `body` control

`#9639` re-points the 9256 controls at a twin (`chatbot-enhanced` / `chatbot-floating`), because the plain `chatbot` face no longer accepts `body` at all. The amended header records this honestly. The consequence is that the plain-`chatbot` row is now a reading **about both channels on one face**, with no same-face control left. Accurate as written; worth a line so the next reader of that table does not take it for a two-sided reading.

## 4 · The render path was not made to agree — different package, different card

`@object-ui/core`'s `validateSchema` / the `SchemaRenderer` path **skips the root parse**, so the retirement of `ChatbotSchema.body` is delivered at parse time (zod) and compile time (tsc) but **not** at render time. Reviewer reproduced this first-hand from source, with null / typeless-child firing controls.

⚠️ This is the shape objectui#8572's own ruling asked about in its last sentence — name the refusal's delivery surface **and whether any consumer path skips the root parse**. One does. ⛔ That does not make the retirement paper: parse-time and compile-time are real surfaces, and `objectui validate` / `objectui check` refuse the document. But an author who never runs either still renders.

⇒ this is the only one of the four with a possible product question in it, and it lands in a different package than #8572's dispatch. ⛔ Not folded into that card.
